0.14.0: `pdf_preview` draws one page as a picture, through `pngFromPdf`, so something can look at what it made. Layout goes wrong silently by nature - a heading stranded at the foot of a page, a table that ran off the side - and `problems` can only report what the writer knew about. This is the first release asking for `RENDER_PDF`, which is why it is a separate call rather than something `fromHtml` does on the way out.
0.13.1: Fixed alongside mermaid: the sandbox shim provides `global`, which the bundled diagram renderer had been left without.
0.11.0: A skill, **Making a PDF**. A run said it plainly - "I don't have any 'how to make a PDF' skill" - and the tool description had nowhere left to put what it needed to say.
0.9.1: jsPDF stops bringing three features this plugin never calls. Measured rather than assumed: the bundle was audited before anything was swapped out.
0.9.0: The embedded font carries the letters the document will set, and no others. Subsetting took a Polish document from roughly 100 ms of font work to 5 ms.
0.8.0: A font is embedded only where the text needs one. `fromHtml` had been timing out at ten seconds on a sentence of English, because it wrote 1.4 MB of TTF into every document whether or not anything needed it. ASCII went from 103 ms to 1 ms.
0.7.0: The agents' tool answers the **key** and not the base64 it names.
0.6.1: No code changed. `category` became `tags` in every manifest here, and a manifest field is a patch.
0.6.0: The agents' `uploadBinary` has nowhere to put bytes; the function still does. A run had answered a png and a key and then written five thousand characters of base64 into the next call by hand.
0.5.0: Mermaid diagrams are drawn into the page as vectors rather than pasted in as pictures.
0.4.0: The bundle carries its own floor. A plugin is read before it is granted anything, so the shim that stands in for the platform's globals has to be inside the file - without it this plugin could not be installed at all.
0.3.0: Optional parameters carry a real default instead of a sentinel. `0` no longer means *the usual number* and an empty string no longer means *use the configured one* - the argument can simply be left out, and the tool descriptions stopped spending a model's attention explaining a convention it kept getting wrong.
0.2.0: No change to this plugin. The repository moved its hashing to the platform's crypto API and versioned everything together.
0.1.0: First release. Lays HTML out as a PDF on A4. Writer, fonts and diagram renderer are all bundled in.
